title: Predictive Inventory Scaling
business: E-commerce logistics providers managing high-velocity warehouse inventory systems.
problem: As the number of unique product SKUs grows, the time required to perform real-time stock lookups increases linearly, causing latency spikes during peak shopping events.
solution: By transitioning from a linear search to a hash-based lookup, we stabilize the time complexity, ensuring that lookup duration remains constant regardless of the total SKU count.
steps: Analyze current lookup operations to identify O(n) linear search patterns.
Implement a hash table data structure to map SKU identifiers to memory addresses.
Refactor retrieval logic to utilize direct key-based access instead of iterating through arrays.
Validate that lookup time remains stable as the SKU dataset expands.
outcome: Consistent response times for inventory queries during high-traffic periods, preventing system bottlenecks.
limitation: Hash tables require additional memory to maintain the hash map structure; this trade-off is verified by monitoring memory usage metrics as the SKU database grows.
